candidates: When documentation code examples reference mermaid via CDN, always include an explicit version pin. In source files under `packages/mermaid/src/docs/` that are processed by the `docs.mts` build transform, use the `<MERMAID_VERSION>` placeholder (which gets substituted at build time). In files that are served or archived directly and do not go through the transform (e.g., standalone HTML in `vdocs/`), hardcode the current major version (e.g., `@9`). Unversioned URLs like `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid/dist/...` cause archived documentation to break when a new major version is released.

CI status badges in README files (including `README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`, `docs/README.md`, and any other README variants) must link to the currently active CI system — GitHub Actions (`https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg`) — and must not reference decommissioned services such as Travis CI. When updating any one README, check that all sibling README variants receive the same badge update.

When adding or reviewing code examples in documentation that reference mermaid module file paths, verify that filenames are correctly spelled — for example, the ESM build artifact is `mermaid.esm.mjs`, not `mermaid.ems.mjs`.

Variables in `packages/mermaid/src/docs.mts` that hold a specific semver component (rather than the full version string) must be named to reflect which component they contain. For example, a variable that stores only the major version should be named `MERMAID_MAJOR_VERSION` (or `mermaidMajorVersion`), not a generic name like `mermaidVersion`, so readers immediately know it does not hold the full semver.
